incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - High OOM rate on inference pods (prod-us-east-1). Autoscaler activity detected. Paging on-call SRE.
Jenna L.: on it. seen the page. shifting to #incidents. @Miguel_R do you have eyes on runtime metrics?
Miguel R.: yes, tailing metrics now. token throughput spiked ~2x at 11:12 UTC then we started seeing container restarts. lots of OOMs on model-serving pods (v2.3.1). suspect autoscale snapback + pod eviction.
Priya S.: seeing node flaps too — nodes going NotReady briefly, kubelet reconnects. could be driver issue or thermal. attaching quick logs below.
Priya S.: ```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep model
model-a-7f9d4    0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   3 (OOMKilled)  5m
model-b-5c1a2    1/1 Running            0             2m
``` 
Miguel R.: logs from a dying pod:
Miguel R.: ```
RuntimeError: CUDARuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 36.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.72 GiB total capacity; 31.42 GiB already allocated)
  File "/srv/runtime/infer.py", line 421, in forward
    out = model.generate(...)
``` 
Marco G.: infra note — the nodes that flapped are g5.12xlarge instances. I see kernel driver restarts around the same time on node ip-10-0-23-45.
Marco G.: `journalctl -k | grep nvidia` shows repeated driver rebinds.
Jenna L.: okay, immediate triage plan:
- mute noisy alerts (gpu_oom_rate) temporarily
- scale down HPA minReplicas to 1 for model-a to stop rapid churn
- cordon any nodes showing driver instability
- pin some traffic to model-b (healthy) via traffic router rules
Jenna L.: @deploy-bot please mute alert gpu_oom_rate for 30m (reason: mitigation in progress)
deploy-bot: Done — alert gpu_oom_rate muted for 30 minutes by Jenna L. (incident 1769965432)
Priya S.: doing cordon on nodes with repeated driver rebinds now
Priya S.: ```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-23-45
kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
``` 
Miguel R.: adding emergency HPA override: `kubectl patch hpa model-a -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 1, "maxReplicas": 4}}'` — this should stop the up/down thrash that seems to cause contention.
Miguel R.: also deployed a temporary runtime flag to reduce batch_size from 16 -> 4 to reduce memory pressure (config pushed to canary infra-hosts).
Sam K.: support: I'm flagging customers with active sessions. Leah, can you draft a short customer message? we need to be careful on wording.
Leah C.: draft for affected hosted API customers:
Leah C.: "We're currently mitigating an infrastructure issue affecting inference latency and availability in us-east-1. We've applied traffic routing and are rolling back autoscale aggressiveness to stabilize. We'll update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."
Nate H.: good. escalate if we see >10% error rate for >15m. Also, Miguel, what's the rollback plan for model-serving version? v2.3.1 seems to coincide with the start of errors.
Miguel R.: v2.3.1 was rolled 3 days ago with a small kernel/kernel-fusion change. I have a rollback image ready (v2.3.0). Holding off until we stabilize node-driver flakiness because repeated pod restarts will just hit the kernel driver again.
Priya S.: noticed GPU memory telemetry shows fragmentation — many short-lived pods allocate/free causing fragmentation + driver's realloc path hits a kernel bug. We'll keep nodes cordoned and migrate workloads off them.
Marco G.: cloud provider confirmed a transient NVidia driver reload on that host due to host OS updates in the maintenance window — they've isolated the host and are reprovisioning.
Jenna L.: timeline so far:
- 11:12 UTC spike in requests
- 11:13 UTC autoscaler spun up +18 pods across cluster
- 11:14-11:20 GPU driver rebinds on 3 nodes -> pod evictions
- 11:20-11:30 crashloops and OOMs start
- 11:33 P1 pager sent
Jenna L.: current mitigation status:
- muted gpu_oom_rate alerts
- cordoned 3 nodes, draining pods
- reduced HPA minReplicas for model-a
- reduced runtime batch size for canaries
- routing 40% traffic to model-b (stable variant)
Miguel R.: one additional immediate fix: setting container `--memory-reservation` to 0.85 of GPU alloc target and enabling aggressive KV cache eviction. Patch applied to canary; pushing prod after 5m of canary stability.
Priya S.: canary looks stable for 4m, no OOMs so far on patched host.
Sam K.: monitoring error rates: 5XXs peaked at 18% at 11:22, now down to ~4%.
Leah C.: sending the customer note now. cc: support ticket auto-created for affected orgs.
Nate H.: good work. next steps: keep nodes cordoned until cloud replaces problematic hosts; prepare postmortem with root cause (driver + autoscaler feedback loop). Also consider autoscaler cooldown increase.
Miguel R.: submitted PR to increase HPA stabilizationWindowSec and autoscaler cooldown to reduce rapid scale down/up. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/492
Jenna L.: handoff: Priya -> Miguel in 30m. Priya, please document node IDs and any repro outputs in the incident doc.
Priya S.: noted. node IDs: ip-10-0-23-45, ip-10-0-27-91, ip-10-0-11-02. saving `journalctl` excerpts and nv-host logs to /var/incidents/1769965432/
incident-bot: Update: cloud provider replaced 2 hosts, driver reloads stopped on remaining nodes. Monitoring continuing.
Miguel R.: pushing rollback to v2.3.0 is no longer necessary; config patches + autoscaler cooldown fixes appear to have stabilized traffic. will keep oncall assigned for 1 hour.
Jenna L.: closing pager? not yet — keep watch for 30m. If error rate <2% for 30m we can resolve.
Sam K.: alerting support to set internal status: investigating -> mitigated (subject to monitoring)
Leah C.: customer updates sent. I'll prepare an FAQ for support with recommended customer messaging and ETA.
Nate H.: postmortem owners: Miguel (runtime), Priya (infra), Jenna (SRE). Add mitigation timeline and follow-ups: autoscaler tuning, node health checks, and release checklist for driver-involving changes.
Jenna L.: thanks everyone. going to summarize in the incident doc and start timeline write-up.
Miguel R.: thumbs up. I'll land the autoscaler PR and schedule a load test to validate new cooldowns before rolling to other regions.
incident-bot: Incident 1769965432 status: monitoring. Severity: P1 -> P2 when <2% 5XX sustained for 30m.
